There is a massive amount of duplicate links being posted. This fragments the conversations and ruins the discussion when every day there is a new thread in multiple subverses pointing to the same articlevideoimage. Lately this results in tons of posts with less than 50 comments, and new ones popping up daily to further hide the previous days conversation.

The comments for identical links could be combinedduplicated to appear in all Share a Link posts that point to the same source. This would generate a lot more discussion, and reduce the amount of duplicate posts by making them redundant. You could still post something to /news and /politics, and the comments would be from people in both areas. If people do not want to discuss the mainfirst posted link, then they could just make a Discuss post with their comments to start a separate discussion.
Combine the comment section of identical links posted to different subverses.

My concern is it will just give people an excuse to X-Post unnecessarily in an effort to get more exposure on their article.

That said, something needs to be done. As a user of v/all I'm going insane.

I don't think this is a good idea, because the point of different subversives is to focus on different topics and themes.

/v/libertarian, /v/politics and /v/news might have extremely different things to say about the same link, and the whole point of having separate communities is erased if their comments sections are merged.

It would be an even worse idea for more directly opposite communities (would /v/theredpill and /v/twoxchromosomes want their comments merged?) or shitposting communities (should /v/soapdoxbanhammer or /v/mickshut comments be merged into everyone else's discussions?)

This would in effect erase the entire concept of the subverse as a community.

Now, merging with in a single subverse? I could see that as being attractive to some, but it is not my favorite solution to this situation:

Personally, I think the "other discussions" button on a link submission that takes the user to a page listing all the other times a given link has been submitted, is ideal:

  • allows separate discussions of identical content in separate communities with separate purposes
  • provides users a way to discover other discussions about the content, then just the one they are currently in
  • Doubles as a "has this been posted before" or "when was this last posted" check.

That would make for some great conversations!

Adding the discussion button would just show how fragmented the conversation is right now, so that would also be a step forward.

That being said, I would agree it should probably be limited to merging discussion links per subverse. That would at least allow conversations about the same link to persist for more than 1 day and 20 comments, like it is now. It would also allow specific areas like /libertarian and/twochromosomes that need "safe spaces" to continue to exist without outside interruption.

Something needs to be done though. There is no point in posting anything but a smartass comment if your attempt to start a conversation is outdated and pushed from view within the hour by multiple duplicate posts.
This is definitely not a good idea. Subs exist for a reason. Two different subverses comments may focus on completely different aspects of the posted link.
